judged.rule: The first sentence sets up two parties or one odd premise, with no greeting, title card or channel intro.
The same test is run twice (two characters or two rounds), or one question is pressed harder each time, and the two runs are visibly comparable.
The expected outcome is said aloud, by the narrator or a character, immediately before the reversal.
The reversal starts between 65% and 80% of the runtime and is shown as a visible outcome, not only told.
The last 10–13 seconds end on one contrastive line ("bukan X, tapi Y" or an equivalent contrast) and nothing asks for a follow, like or comment.
One narrator carries all lines; character dialogue is read by the same voice and shown as a speech bubble.
Shots change with narration clauses, mostly 2–5 seconds each; hard cuts are the default and at most five whip or slide transitions appear.
Each shot holds one or two outlined bean figures or one object on a flat stage with open sky; nothing important sits inside the caption band.
Captions are lowercase groups of one to three words centred near y 1500, with only the spoken word in the orange box.
The story, characters and wording are original and do not retell a reference episode.
